newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-China will back HK banks, says leading banker.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-China will back HK banks, says leading banker.

text.p: Leading Hong Kong banker, Hang Seng Bank Ltd chief executive Alexander Au, said on Thursday he was confident the Chinese government would rescue any state bank operating in Hong Kong in the event of a financial crisis.

"We don't detect any situation that would lead us to concern," Au told a business seminar in Melbourne when asked about the potential for a banking crisis in Hong Kong after the territory reverts to Chinese rule next July 1.
"China has never failed on its international obligations and I take a lot of comfort from that particular point.
"In other words, if there's anything that might lead to a crisis involving a PRC bank operating in Hong Kong, I don't think that China will not come to their rescue," he added.

Au stressed his comments were hypothetical and that state-owned Chinese banks in Hong Kong were regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), which enjoyed good relations with Beijing and would continue to supervise the banking sector after the handover.
"The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is maintaining an extremely close and friendly relationship with the People's Bank of China," Au said.

China has strived to develop its banking system, Au said, noting that the People's Bank of China was taking advice from the HKMA and the U.S. Federal Reserve to develop its own real-time growth settlement system for next year.
Australian businessmen attending the forum, hosted by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, have expressed concern about the future of Hong Kong as a regional financial centre after the handover.
In particular, one delegate voiced concern about the burden of non-performing loans on China's state banks.
